text_scope: Checks run over every text field in body (paragraph text, list items, callout title and text, heading text) plus title and deck, unless a check says otherwise. The final Sources list is excluded from word_count and forbidden_patterns but included in url checks.

deterministic.message: Post does not match the schema.
Body must be 450-1,100 words, excluding the Sources list.
Too many words per cited fact. The post is padded; cut rather than stretch.
No em or en dashes. Use a comma, colon or full stop.
' , ' or ' - ' left where a dash was removed. Rewrite the sentence.
No exclamation marks.
No emojis.
Hype word. State the fact instead.

deterministic.pattern: (in today's fast-paced|ever[- ]evolving|it's worth noting|it is worth noting|let's dive|dive in|in conclusion|buckle up|\bdelve|tapestry|navigate the complexities|in the world of)
deterministic.message: Filler phrase. Cut it.

deterministic.pattern: ^(this article|this post|in this post|in this article)
deterministic.message: Do not open a paragraph by referring to the post itself.
Every number in the post must appear verbatim in the fact sheet. This is the main anti-fabrication gate.
Every link must point to a URL in the fact sheet's sources.
A block cites a fact ID that is not in the fact sheet.
A block states a number but cites no fact.
Link at least 2 distinct sources.
The post must end with a level-2 'Sources' heading and one list linking every cited source.
The first block must be the lead paragraph.
Use 3-6 level-2 headings, including 'Sources'.
The title states the development. It is not a question.
Slug already exists on the blog.

grounding.5: Every factual claim traces to a fact, at its stated certainty.
grounding.3: Mostly grounded, but one or two claims are stronger than the facts or unsupported.
grounding.1: Claims, numbers or names appear that are not in the fact sheet.

synthesis.5: Connects the sources into a clear picture a reader could not get from any one story.
synthesis.3: Accurate, but reads as a list of story summaries.
synthesis.1: Misreads the facts or presents one source's view as consensus.

voice.5: Calm, plain, specific. Reads like a sharp colleague, not a model.
voice.3: Mostly on voice, with some generic or marketing phrasing.

value.5: A busy engineer learns something useful and knows what to watch.
value.3: Informative but restates the news without adding understanding.
value.1: Padded or repetitive, with nothing a reader would miss.

structure.5: The lead states the development, headings are specific, there is a 'What to watch' section and a Sources list.
structure.3: Workable, with generic headings or a buried lead.

judged.pass_rule: verdict is 'pass', no blocking issues, and every criterion at or above its threshold.

on_failure: One revision (config.max_revisions). If the deterministic checks or the judged rubric still fail after it, the run ends with no post, and the run report records why. Never publish a failing post.
